'''''Daucus pusillus''''' is a species of [[Daucus|wild carrot]] known by the common names '''American wild carrot'''<ref>{{PLANTS|id=DAPU3|taxon=Daucus pusillus|accessdate=17 January 2016}}</ref> and '''rattle-snake-weed'''.<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> Its Latin name means "little carrot", or "tiny carrot". It is similar in appearance to other species and subspecies of wild carrot, with [[umbel]]s of white or pinkish flowers.<ref name=":0">''Jepson Manual''. 1993. [http://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/eflora/eflora_display.php?tid=22395 Jepson Manual Treatment: ''Daucus pusillus'']</ref> The [[taproot]]s are small, edible carrots. It should not be confused with ''[[Conium maculatum]]'', which is highly poisonous.<ref>{{Cite web |title=PlantFiles: The Largest Plant Identification Reference Guide - Dave's Garden |url=https://davesgarden.com/guides/pf/go/74985 |access-date=2024-10-29 |website=davesgarden.com}}</ref>

== Distribution and habitat ==
''Daucus pusillus'' has a [[Antitropical distribution|amphitropical distribution]], and is found in both [[North America|North]] and [[South America]]. This is a common plant found in North America in the [[Southern United States]] and along the west coast from [[Baja California]] to [[British Columbia]]. In South America, this species is found in southern [[Brazil]], northern and central [[Argentina]], and [[Chile]].<ref>{{Cite book  |title=Catálogo de las plantas vasculares del Cono Sur. volumen 2: Dicotyledoneae: Acanthaceae - Fabaceae (Abarema - Schizolobium) |date=2008 |publisher=Missouri Botanical Garden Press |isbn=978-1-930723-70-2 |editor-last=Zuloaga |editor-first=Fernando O. |series=Monographs in systematic botany from the Missouri Botanical Garden |volume=2 |location=St. Louis, Mo |page=1069 |oclc=294820637 |editor-last2=Morrone |editor-first2=Osvaldo |editor-last3=Belgrano |editor-first3=Manuel J. |editor-last4=Missouri Botanical Garden |editor-last5=Instituto de Botánica Darwinion (San Isidro, Argentina)}}</ref> It grows in rocky or sandy places.<ref name=":0" />
